$comment: Bounty connector definition. Muse publishes no file format for connectors; this holds what its connector guidelines and submission form ask for (endpoint, authentication, scopes, credentials, tool documentation with each tool classified), in one place. Generated from the hosted connector's tools/list by build-connector.mjs.
name: Bounty
summary: Tells a shopper what a purchase at a store earns, from the store's own published declaration, and finds stores where a purchase earns.
description: Bounty reads any store's Open Bounty Schema declaration: the small public object a store publishes at /.well-known/bounty.json, or points to with <link rel="bounty">, saying what a purchase earns the shopper (points, store credit, tokens or perks). get_bounty returns the store's own sentence, exactly as published, the resolved object, and whether it is signed; a store that publishes nothing is reported as unknown, never as "no". search_stores searches the Bounty index of 6,000+ stores where a purchase earns. The index is an open registry any store can enter by publishing a declaration.

mcp.self_host_note: The self-host template serves get_bounty only; search_stores reads the hosted index.

data.reads: get_bounty: a store's own public declaration (/.well-known/bounty.json or its rel="bounty" link target), its home page head, and, if a product URL is given, that product page. search_stores: the Bounty index.
data.writes: Nothing on anyone's behalf. A store whose own declaration checks valid is recorded in the open registry (its domain and the public fields of its declaration), so search_stores can find it.
data.personal_data: None. The inputs are a store domain, a product URL or a search keyword; nothing about the person asking is received or stored.
data.retention: Check results are cached for 5 minutes per store. Registry entries lapse after 90 days without a fresh valid check. No request logs.

tools.name: get_bounty
tools.title: Get a store's bounty
tools.description: Read what buying at a store earns the shopper, from the store's own published Open Bounty Schema declaration (its /.well-known/bounty.json, or the object its <link rel="bounty"> points to). Returns status (valid, invalid or unknown), earn_display (the store's own sentence, exactly as published), the program, the resolved object, where it was found and whether it is signed. "unknown" means the store publishes no declaration; it does not mean purchases earn nothing. Read-only.

product.description: Optional: an https product page URL on that domain, to check whether that product is covered

tools.name: search_stores
tools.title: Search the store index
tools.description: Search the Bounty index of 6,000+ stores where a purchase earns, by store name or keyword. The index is an open registry any store can enter by publishing a declaration: a store whose own Open Bounty Schema declaration checks valid is added beside the NCTR Alliance listings. Returns up to 10 matches in alphabetical order, each with its slug, name, earn_display (the earn sentence), program, listed_by (store: the store declares it; program: the program that pays it declares it; index: the index lists it) and verification, plus total, the number of matches. get_bounty checks any store directly. Read-only.

query.description: A store name or keyword, e.g. "outfitters"
